Variants.Content: Odivo lies in eastern Myr and the Disputed Lands, politically situated within the city-state of Myr and the trade routes of the lower Rhoyne. It is a castle mainly responsible for local garrison, tax collection and sheltering the nearby population. Walls and roads tied the surrounding population, storage, and garrison here; even if the flags were changed, this stronghold would still affect how nearby people paid taxes, traded, and sought refuge.
Entry Odivo Keep Local families also relied on dyes, glass, weaving, orchards, and ever-rerouted trade travel; any time a road, well, or dock failed, the price fell first to them.

Entry Odivo Keep They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of Myr and disputed lands; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, and true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hooves.

Entry Odivo Keep If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Artisans measure Odivo's stone walls, wooden beams, iron gates, crypts, and the seams left by generations of repairs with their own hands, while priests carry on through ritual the temples of the gods, guild traditions, and old walls left by the wars of the Free Cities. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Odivo Keep They care about dyes, glass, weaving, orchards, and the ever-changing trade routes. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
